legend: Tolerances: a D or T target is checked to +-10 mm (section 04) unless its line prints another bound; P, E and W values carry their own stated error (check EW: a check that reads one prints it with its class and error from the anchors file, and the open item 'checks on estimated values' names it in that check's clause). Classes: D drawing, T table or text, P photo proportion, E estimated, W web.
abbreviations: Abbreviations: GLB (binary GL Transmission Format, GL = Graphics Library), JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), MB (megabytes), ID (identifier), mm (millimetres), mm3 (cubic millimetres), deg (degrees), vs (versus), trans and rot (translation and rotation, motion types of the anchors files), p. (page), Fig. (figure), OM (operating manual of this variant), OM/, DOC/, PH/ and ART/ (the folders of the operating manual, the other documents, the machine photos and the memory block's artifacts, as the header of sources.md writes them out), DTPEW (the five classes D, T, P, E, W), DECISION n (a ruling of the meta orchestrator of the workflow). [1] to [12] are the checks of section 04, [8e] (envelope boxes) and [9x] (the other motions) belong to checks 8 and 9; [B1], [B2], [B3], [D2], [N], [EW] and [V] are the script's own checks, EW standing for values of class E or W (P counts with them). M7, G3a, SS5 and the like are rows of a spec's measure table (measure_list.md lists them); Q1, S28, Y01, OA1 and the like are device designations of the electrical legend (wiring set 568-70.9001) and of the hydraulic parts list. Quoted sources use the specs' own source keys, for example P6, P7 or P36 (OM page 6, 7 or 36), P37f (OM p.37, Fig. 7.1 front view close-up), F412, F63 and F81 (OM Figs. 4.1.2, 6.3 and 8.1), PLAN (OM Fig. 4.2.2, the foundation plan), CERT (certificate of this machine), OLD-I (Fig. I of the Russian manual of the older relay variant), PH-cross1 (one machine photo): a key means what its own spec says, and each spec's keys with the files they resolve to are listed in sources.md, section 'Source keys of each spec and the files they resolve to'.
